text.insert: Implementation concisely maps the system design to the codebase. It follows the code's structure, explains the key reasons behind its implementation, and links to the design and source for further detail.

Use actual package and module names. Each page connects its code area to the design it realizes, explains meaningful choices, and points to the relevant source. A short paragraph with links may be enough.

rows: Name the system responsibility or agent contract this code implements and link to its owning document.
Explain consequential library choices, module boundaries, patterns, and constraints. Preserve known reasons and relevant tradeoffs.
Link to the actual files, related modules, and source-level explanations needed to continue reading.

text.insert: Mirror meaningful subdivisions of the codebase. Add detail only when it improves orientation or explains a choice the reader cannot otherwise understand. A page does not need a rule governing future code to be useful.

System Design owns behavior, state, and contracts. Agents owns agent definitions, context, tools, outputs, and responsibilities. Implementation may explain shared agent machinery and how it realizes those contracts. File-local detail stays in source comments.

Verify the code before describing the implementation. Record supported rationale without inventing rejected alternatives. Mark proposed behavior as proposed. Preserve important contracts and reasons in their owning documents when shortening or moving content.

The section helps a reader move between an understanding of the system and its actual implementation. Concise explanations and precise links retain that connection without duplicating the design or narrating every file.
